title.en: Name of the terminology, preferably in English. An English abstract is sufficient as an alternative. Language can be selected or detected automatically

abbreviation.en: Common, unique abbreviation, acronym, or notation the terminology is known under

identifier.en: Alternative URIs the terminology is identified by (e.g. Wikidata URI)

definition.en: Short terminology description, preferably in English. An English title is also sufficient. For copied text, use quotation marks and keep the original language. Language can be selected or detected automatically

media.en: URLs of logos or other images representing the terminology

size.en: Number of classes, subclasses, taxa, terms, concepts etc. Please add date in parenthesis (YYYY-MM)

kosTypes.en: Type of KOS, such as a classification scheme, thesaurus, or ontology, searchable by name or through the hierarchy

subjects.en: Subjects from DDC, EuroVoc, and ILC, searchable by term or by browsing the hierarchy

versionOf.en: Terminology to which this version belongs, searchable by title

basedOn.en: Terminology on which this terminology is based, searchable by title

replacedBy.en: Terminology that replaces this terminology, searchable by title

created.en: The year when the KOS was first created (YYYY)

license.en: License under which the terminology is available, searchable or selectable from the hierarchy of licences

url.en: Web address of the terminology's homepage

additionalLinks.en: Links to additional resources related to the terminology, such as documentation, downloads, or project websites

distributions.en: Files and publication locations where this terminology is available

issueTracker.en: Where issues about this terminology are managed

formats.en: Formats in which the terminology is available, searchable or selectable from the hierarchy of formats

access.en: How the terminology can be accessed, such as freely online, with registration, or through a licensed database

publisher.en: Publisher of the terminology and its URI, preferably an institution rather than a person

address.en: Address of the terminology publisher, especially the country

contact.en: Email address of anyone in charge of the terminology

listedIn.en: Terminology registries in which the terminology is listed, searchable or selectable by name from the terminology registry list

api.en: Web services providing access to the terminology, including the service URL and API type

displayOptions.en: Options for displaying terminology concepts, including hiding notations and sorting them numerically

namespace.en: Namespace used to identify concepts in the terminology

notationPattern.en: Pattern describing the structure of concept notations

uriPattern.en: Pattern used to construct concept URIs from their notations

exampleNotations.en: Examples of concept notations, separated by commas
